 Need for revenue authorities in India to shift focus from income tax to expenditure tax 
 Homeyar Jal Tavaria in Spreading Light …. / Oct 23, 2026, 08:59 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print We are aware that Income Tax as mandated by law and implemented in India is a retrograde and unfair tax. The reasons being: 1. All income earners are not treated equally. Agriculture income earners get a full exemption regardless of their income earnings from agricultural activity. The rich and wealthy are able to create tax structures that protect their income from income tax. 2. There is double taxation - savings are taxed again as income. As an individual you get small business profits or salary income on which income tax is paid. Those savings are put into investments into shares, corporate debentures, bank deposits, etc. Income from these is taxed again. Surprisingly, corporates investing into other corporates have a benefit of intercorporate dividends exemption to a large extent but individual income tax payers have no such benefits under income tax law of India. This is why we have such a low percentage income tax returns submission compared to the numbers of PAN Card holders in India. It can be safely presumed that there is income tax leakage when income tax returns are not submitted. There is a need to change focus in India from income tax to expenditure tax. This needs to be very well thought out and validated by data available with the Finance Ministry. The biggest advantage of doing away with individual income tax in my view would be deletion of the concept of 'black money'. Black money was / is money on which no income tax was paid by individuals. Originally, that had some moral and ethical concerns but today the clack mark on black money is gone. It’s presence is takin in stride and we have learnt to live with it. When conceptually, there is no income tax payable the concept and idea of money being 'black' falls. The distinction between black (no income tax paid) and white (income tax paid) money gets deleted. Expenditure Act is separate but parallel like Railway tracks with GST. Proper implementation will improve GST collection also. This absence of income tax increases the amount available with individuals for expenditure and savings. Savings are not in the nature of expenditure and those transactions must not be caught in the ambit of Expenditure tax. The type and nature of the savings investments are based on individual risk profiles. As compared to the very limited pool of full income tax payer/ ITR filers, the pool of expenditure to base tax collection workings is significantly larger. The tax collection structure must be strengthened because the expense tax payers and tax collectors population would greatly increase. This should result in tax buoyancy. We have to create an IT software enabled system by which every individual has an Expense Recognition code on the same lines as a PAN card. In fact, the PAN Card number gets replaced by Expense Recognition Code. So, the efforts of linking Aadhar number with PAN Card number does not go waste. Many in India possess PAN Cards, so there will not be any great effort. Even for Expenditure Tax, the PAN Card can be used at the transaction point. Currently, we are very pleased at the individual income tax collections that are shown in the Budget Revenue Statement. However, these collections are on a very narrow base of salaried employees, pensioners and retirees. This base will shrink due to persons aging. There is evidence that formal employment is not rising as fast as it should and we will see individual income tax collections reaching a plateau and then declining in future. The success of expense tax collection thru expense recognition code / PAN Card number comes from: 1. The individual (minors get linked with an adult) submits his Expense Recognition Code when he incurs any Expense and this code is printed on the bill / invoice that the counter party gives for delivery of goods / services; 2. Every month / quarter the individual can have a look at the IT system to know what is the amount of expenditure tax that he has paid and the person / parties to whom the person has paid the expense tax. 3. At the software end, a cumulative ledger of tax payers and tax collectors has to be kept. It is the duty of the software programme to identify the total tax collection by the Expense Tax Collector and the amount deposited with the Government of India. Besides the time difference of collection and payment to Treasury there should not be any major value difference. If there is, it is identified who has collected the Expense Tax but not paid to the Treasury; 4. Every quarter end there has to be a certain percentage of Expense Tax paid (say 20 - 30%) refunded to the linked savings bank account of the expense tax payer, in the next month. This fixed % of auto refund must not change and the expense tax payer does not need to file any Returns. This refund mechanism is necessary so all individuals collect their bills / invoices and nothing sells without bill / invoice in support. A lot of business gets done on the premise of non-collection of tax. Refund of payment would help. In my view, this is a simple expense tax structure where the Government Tax collection department keeps track of goods / service providers who collect the tax but do not pay it into the Treasury. This has to be the focus of Expense Tax Administration. Any tax structure should not have material imbalances in applicability. The Income Tax Act of India is an imbalanced and unfair tax. All must get caught in the tax net so that tax collections are buoyant. In some ways, the expense tax concept links tax collection with GDP much better than income tax does. To it’s advantage, the tax is fair to all and there are no complaints of tax favouritism. This expense tax concept also removes the ugly label of significant 'black economy' that India carries. In fact, if we create a good structure to support the idea of Expense tax (IT system, bureaucracy reorganization, education of consumers / businesses / tax professionals), we would be pioneers in this matter as we have been in Jan Dhan accounts and Direct Benefits Transfers (DBT) into individual savings bank accounts. This is an idea worth working on and putting into place at the earliest.
